# Casberi — Full documentation

> Your life and money are scattered across apps. Casberi gives you an inbox and a wallet for all your accounts: connect your apps and everything lands in one private feed on your device, beside one balance for every account you have and follow. Free on iPhone, iPad and Mac, with no Casberi account, ever.

Website: https://casberi.app · Docs: https://casberi.app/docs.html · App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/casberi/id6788637831 · Privacy: https://casberi.app/privacy.html

Last updated: October 26, 2026

## Features — everything you can do

### Just connect

- Own your data — No account, no sign-in. It's all on your device.
- Connect your apps — Mail, photos, wallets, calendars and a hundred more, kept in Library.
- Watch one feed — Every app together, a category at a time, or one app on its own.

### Keep tabs

- Every subscription — What renews and when, found on its own. What it costs, in the Wallet.
- Follow your accounts — Balances, holdings, spending and threats. Following is read-only.
- Private by default — No server, no analytics, and every wallet read goes through Tor on iPhone and iPad.

### Take action

- An account of your own — No phrase to write down. A recovery key in iCloud Keychain, and a co-signer if you want one.
- Move money — Swap, send, receive, sweep or buy a gift card. Face ID approves every move.
- Save and find anything — Share from any app or take a screenshot. Search finds it by what it says.

### Make it yours

- Make it yours — Your name and photo, Feed order, widgets, theme, notifications, and where your data lives.

## How to use — the whole app

### Just connect

#### Start here

1. Open it. There's no account and nothing to sign up for. The first screen is a demo — one person's furnished life you can walk through. Tap Exit demo and none of it sticks.
2. Tap Library, the tab that wears your face. Start with any of these leads it: an app, a calendar, a card, a subscription, or an account to follow.
3. Pick one and connect it. Calendar and Photos are one tap; an account needs only an address.
4. Tap Feed. What you connected is there.

That's the whole setup. Add more apps whenever you like.

#### Words we use

- A thing is one item in your feed: a photo, an email, a post, a payment, a renewal.
- The tabs are the five buttons at the bottom: Feed, Wallet, Move, Library and Search.
- A category is a group of apps — Day, Notes, Social, Work, Media, Life, Agents — read together as one section of the Feed, or one app at a time. The Wallet has a tab of its own.
- A door is a row that opens a page. The page's title is its way back: "Wallet · Holdings" returns to Holdings.
- Your account is the one account Casberi made you, which you can move money from. Following is every other account you read.
- A widget is Casberi on your Home Screen: your notes, your wallet, or your feed.

#### Five tabs

Casberi is five tabs, each answering one question. Feed is what's happening. Wallet is what you have. Move is what you do with it. Library is your apps and you. Search finds anything.

Read down a page and the bar folds into one circle; scroll back up or tap the circle and the five return. Nothing that picks or goes back sits at the top edge: a page's choices stand under its box, and its title takes you back. On iPad and Mac the same five run down the rail, and ⌘1 to ⌘5 open them.

#### Feed

The Feed is every app together. Its box leads with the newest thing. Under it, Newest lists the five newest things, whatever day they came. Then a section per category — Day and Notes first, then Social, Work, Media, Life and Agents — each holding today's rows, one row per app.

A section's name is a door to the whole category, newest first; tap an app for just that app. Its + adds what fits: an event or a reminder in Day, a note or a voice note in Notes. Day is what's ahead: meetings, reminders and renewals, in date order. The Wallet isn't in the Feed — it has its own tab. Change the sections' order under Feed order in Casberi's settings.

#### Library

Library is everything you have, and its tab wears your face. Its box counts eight kinds — Apps, Calendars, Cards, Contacts, Mail lists, Media, Subscriptions and Wallet — and each count is a button: press one to list that kind. Casberi's own settings come first, then a folder for each category with its apps.

Tap an app you have and its feed rises. Hold it for Open and Settings; on its page, the sliders beside its name open its settings. Apps is the whole catalog, A–Z, with what you've added marked. Contacts is everyone you deal with, from every app.

Over a hundred apps, connecting three ways: one tap for the Apple apps you already use (Photos, Calendar, Reminders, Health, Music, Contacts, Apple Wallet); a sign-in or a pasted token for services (Gmail, GitHub, Notion, Linear, and more); and nothing at all for accounts — type an address.

### Keep tabs

#### Subscriptions

Every subscription is in Library, under Subscriptions, with the day it renews. Casberi finds them on its own — a charge that repeats at one price, from your cards, Apple Wallet or Rocket Money — and you can add any it missed with Track a subscription.

What they cost lives in one place: the Wallet's Spending, behind its Subscriptions door, with the month's total and a calendar of renewals. The mailing lists that write to you are in Library, under Mail lists, each with a way out. To follow a calendar you don't own, paste its link — webcal:// or an .ics — under Library › Calendars. Its events land in Day.

#### Wallet

The Wallet is every account you have and follow, added up. Follow an account from its +: an address, ENS, .sol or basename. Or connect a wallet app or an exchange.

Following is read-only. The connection asks for zero permissions, so following an account can never trade or move funds. Name as many accounts as you like; follow up to five.

The Wallet is four tiles. Home leads with your balance and its line, then its doors: Account (your account's keys and settings), Needs you (every ask, from every page), Permissions (approvals and delegations — who can spend from you) and Threats (address poisoning, fake tokens, fake transfers). Activity is every transaction, by day. Holdings is what the money is: on All, the apps that made you a wallet, then Tokens, Positions and NFTs; its doors show their top three. A loan says how far the price can fall. Spending is the week or the month against the last one to the same day, behind four doors: Subscriptions, Places, Fees (what your sends paid the network) and Round-ups (what your change bought). Fees and round-ups stay out of the total.

Every box carries one switch, Yours · Following · All, whenever there are two to choose: your account alone, the accounts you follow, or everything added up. Flip it on one tile and every tile follows.

An approval you once gave an app is one tap from a cancellation Casberi prepares. Your own wallet app does the signing — or, for your Casberi account, Revoke takes it back right there. If you make this device an owner of a Safe, tapping Sign sends that one signature to Safe's own service after Face ID. It can never execute a transaction on its own.

If you use DeFi: the Wallet also carries Aave and Morpho health, Uniswap positions in or out of range, Hyperliquid liquidation distance, Aerodrome locks and their weekly vote deadline, staked ETH and HYPE, exchange balances and validators — all in one total. A Safe reads as a Safe: owners, threshold, signature queue. MetaMask Card, ether.fi and Plasma One card spends, Peer onramp fills, 0xBow deposits clearing and Railgun shields land as ordinary rows. Spam folds into a pile you can mute.

### Take action

#### Your account

Casberi can make you an account of your own — tap Create an account on the Wallet, or open Move. It lives on Base, Ethereum and Robinhood. There's no phrase to write down, and Casberi never holds it: only your keys can move it. Creating it walks four steps:

1. A recovery key in iCloud Keychain. If you lose this device, your account opens on another.
2. A co-signer in another wallet, if you want one. That wallet signs once to prove it can, and co-signs any move over your spend limit.
3. A spend limit, with a co-signer: moves over an amount of each coin a month need the co-signer too. Getting your account back needs it too.
4. Round-ups. Each send, swap or gift card rounds up to the next $1 or $5, and once the change reaches $5 it buys ETH, or a token you pick, with the move that gets it there.

Its page, Wallet › Account, holds the Keys — This iPhone, Recovery key, Co-signer, Networks, Tor, Private key — and Spending: Spend limit and Round-ups. This device's key changes with every send.

The change waits in your dollar, counted per network. A token on the same network is bought on Uniswap or Aerodrome; one on another network, through Relay. A send signed under your spend limit can't buy, so its change waits for your next move. A swap buys only when it sells your dollar, and a gift card's change is counted once it's paid. What the change bought is in Spending, under Round-ups.

Once a month, Needs you asks you to check your recovery key: Face ID and a test signature, no fee, nothing sent, and a page saying the networks where it works. Export creates a new private key, adds it as an owner and shows it once, so the account opens in another wallet without Casberi. Nodes reads your account from your own node, each address checked against its network first.

#### Move

Move rises as a tray over wherever you are. You say what you want as a sentence and fill in its blanks; the slider under it sets the amount. Move opens on Swap. Its verbs, A–Z:

- Buy a gift card from Bitrefill, by category and merchant, paid from your account in USDC on Base.
- Receive picks its network and copies your address. Someone on another network can send a coin Relay bridges, and it lands as the one you pick. From another wallet connects a wallet of yours, and you approve each send into your account there.
- Send an amount of a token to an address or a name, on a network. Add puts another in the same transaction.
- Swap one token for another, on one network or across two.
- Sweep swaps every token under $1, or $5, on one network for ETH, in one transaction.

Swap goes straight to the exchanges. Your phone asks every Uniswap pool on Base, Ethereum and Robinhood, and Aerodrome's on Base, takes the best price, and writes the swap itself. No aggregator stands in between. The foot names the exchange and its pool fee — "On Uniswap · 0.05% pool fee" — and the pool fee is in the price. The swap is refused before Face ID unless you get at least the quote less 0.5%, or 0.3% on Ethereum. The tokens come from Uniswap's list, and a pasted contract works too. WETH and ETH swap one for one, with no pool and no fee but the network's. With a spend limit on, every swap needs your co-signer too.

To another network, pick the network for what you get. The swap crosses through Across: ETH arrives as ETH, and USDC as USDC (USDG on Robinhood); anything else is swapped into one of them first, in the same transaction. The foot says Across's fee and about how long it takes. Your phone writes the deposit into Across's own contract and reads the other network until it arrives, and Activity shows the crossing as one row. If no relayer fills it in time, Across's contract refunds it on the network it left — ETH comes back as WETH, which Swap turns back into ETH.

Sweep lists every token on the network worth less than the line, priced off the pools, ten at a time. What stays is listed under it, with why: no price, not on Uniswap's list (most dust is sent by strangers), it holds your round-ups, no pool trades it, or it would return less than half of what it's worth. Tap a row to leave it out. One Face ID signs the lot, and a sweep whose network fee is more than it returns isn't signed.

Before Face ID asks, the grey line says the most the fee can be. Details shows the whole move, one line a row — who it goes to, the fee, the exchange and its pool fee, what you get at least — and whether this exact move was simulated and lands as written. What it showed is what Face ID signs.

A warning takes the grey line's place: this would fail, the address is sanctioned (OFAC) or reported (GoPlus), it looks like an address you've paid, it's a new contract, or it's your first send there. On a warning the verb reads Send anyway: the first tap arms it, the second signs.

#### Notes

Notes, a section of the Feed, holds everything you write: your own notes, and what Obsidian, Notion, Day One and Apple Journal hold. Your notes' page — All, Folders, Voice — is in Library's Notes folder. Check off a list, record a voice note, attach a picture or a sketch, file into folders, or lock one. A passage you keep from anything you read lands here as a highlight.

#### Open a thing

Tap any row to open it. From there, open it in the app it came from, or share it. Tags arrive on their own, so there is nothing to file.

Some rows let you act in place: start an email, put an event on your calendar, turn a note into a reminder. Each write asks first. A row that came from Calendar or Reminders opens there to change it. Casberi keeps tabs; your own apps do the work.

#### Save and find

Share from any app and it lands in your feed. Screenshots flow in on their own and become searchable by what's in them. Voice notes transcribe.

Save to Casberi in Control Center opens the composer from anywhere — paste something to save it, or tap the mic and talk. Typing alone never saves. Casberi note starts a note.

To find a thing again, tap Search and type: apps, accounts, people, notes, subscriptions and your things stand under their categories, and a tap goes there. Find, its last row, searches your things by what they say. Spotlight finds them too.

Three widgets, each a small tile: Notes shows your two newest notes, Wallet your balance and its line, and Feed how many things came today in each category.

#### Privacy and Tor

There is no Casberi server and no analytics. Your apps are read straight from your device.

On iPhone and iPad, every request that names a wallet — yours or one you follow — goes through Tor, always, with one circuit per wallet. No service learns where you are, or that the wallets you look at are one person's. The Feed's apps never go through Tor. Swaps, sweeps and Across go through Tor. A few services refuse Tor and are read directly: Relay, GeckoTerminal, and the public nodes of Tenderly, Optimism, Gnosis Chain and Plasma. So Receive from another network, and a round-up bought on another network, say "not through Tor". The Mac has no Tor yet, and says so.

What this app reaches, in Casberi's settings under Data, lists every service Casberi can reach and what it actually reached, by category, including how much went through Tor and which services refuse it.

### Make it yours

#### Your options

Casberi's own settings lead Library: your photo and name, your data, Feed order, theme, notifications, language, support and licenses.

Your data is all on your device. Export, import, or delete it anytime, and turn iCloud sync on if you want it.

Notifications are two switches, Wallet and Feed. They arrive as Casberi finds them, one per app.

An agent you bring — Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Venice, Bankr, OpenRouter, Grok, NEAR AI or Muse — connects from Library like every other app. Its key lives in the Keychain, and what it sends goes from your device straight to that provider, billed to you. Your own model is a server you run that speaks OpenAI's format: give its address, a key only if it asks for one, and pick a model. Apple Intelligence needs no key. In the composer, the agent you connected is picked; Send asks it, and if it fails, it says so. There is no Casberi server in between.

#### If something's missing

- I connected an app and nothing showed up — Pull down on the feed to refresh. If it's an Apple app, check iOS Settings → Casberi and make sure you said yes. Some apps are honestly quiet: Trello, for instance, only shows cards actually assigned to you, and the app tells you so.
- My screenshots aren't updating — Photos needs full access, not selected photos. iOS Settings → Casberi → Photos → All Photos. That's also what lets a screenshot you delete in Photos disappear here.
- My account shows no balance — Give the first read a moment, then pull to refresh. Pick Following on the Wallet's switch and check the address. Naming an account is free; following is capped at five.
- My wallets aren't refreshing — On iPhone and iPad, wallet reads go through Tor, and a network that blocks Tor holds them back. Each wallet keeps its last reading, stamped. Your account's page shows Tor as On, Connecting, or Can't connect.
- A subscription is missing — Casberi only counts a charge once it has repeated at the same price, about a month apart. Connect the card or Apple Wallet it's paid from, or add it yourself with Track a subscription in Library.

## Every app

Over a hundred apps, in nine catalog categories: Wallet, Testnets, Work, Agents, Day, Notes, Life, Social and Media. The full list, each with one line, is on https://casberi.app/docs.html#every-app.

## Questions, answered

- Do I need an account? — No. There's nothing to sign up for — Casberi works the moment it's installed.
- Where do my things live? — In a database on your device. No Casberi server holds them, and iCloud sync stays off until you turn it on. Deleting is two clear choices: Delete things wipes your data (this device and iCloud); Delete access removes every token and key Casberi holds.
- What does it cost? — It's free on the App Store.
- What do I need to run it? — An iPhone, iPad, or Mac. Nothing is billed, and no question goes to a model unless you connect an agent and send to it — then it goes straight to that provider, or to your own server. Connected apps do reach their own services to fetch your things; that traffic goes from your device to them, never through a Casberi server.
- Does Casberi hold my money? — No. Your account is a Safe that only your keys can move: this device's key, a recovery key in your iCloud Keychain, and a co-signer in another wallet if you add one. Export a private key and the account opens in another wallet without Casberi.
- Can it act without asking? — No. Typed text never saves silently, and any write that leaves the app waits for a tap. Following an account is read-only — it can never trade or move funds. Your account moves money only when you finish a sentence in Move and approve it with Face ID; over your spend limit, your co-signer signs too, and a round-up buys only inside a move you approved. A Safe signature leaves only when you tap Sign and pass Face ID, and can never execute a transaction on its own. Bankr is only ever asked questions, never given instructions.
